answer:
Here is what your records suggest bringing up at your check-up, most important first.

1. A positive stool test (FIT) from 4 November 2025. Your records show a positive result and no colonoscopy or other follow-up test since. A positive FIT normally needs a colonoscopy to look for the cause, such as polyps or cancer. Please ask whether this was followed up. If it was not, this is the most urgent item.

2. Your HbA1c (blood sugar average) is due. The last one was 6.9% on 16 February 2026, down from 8.3% in January 2025. Nothing has been recorded since, which is over eight months ago.

3. Your LDL ("bad") cholesterol was 131 mg/dL on 18 February 2025, which is high. Atorvastatin was prescribed two days later, and there is no cholesterol test since. Ask for a lipid panel to see how the statin is working.

4. Your kidney function (eGFR) fell from 73 to 69 over the year. It is still in the normal range, but the trend is worth checking. No urine albumin test is recorded. People with diabetes usually have this checked yearly, so ask about it.

5. Metformin was stopped in April 2024, and the records do not say why. Your HbA1c rose after that. Ask your doctor for the reason and whether your current diabetes plan still fits.

6. No diabetic eye exam or foot exam is recorded. Ask about both. They may have happened somewhere that is not in these records.

7. No vaccines are recorded at all. Ask about flu, pneumonia, shingles and tetanus boosters. Vaccines given at a pharmacy may not appear here.

8. Nothing to act on here: the chest CT angiogram in July 2025 showed no pulmonary embolism, and the chest wall pain has resolved. The raised D-dimer blood test from that time is explained by the normal CT result.
short: Positive stool test (FIT) in Nov 2025 with no follow-up colonoscopy recorded. HbA1c not checked since Feb 2026. LDL 131 mg/dL with no recheck since starting a statin. No urine albumin test, diabetic eye or foot exam, or vaccines recorded.
